text:
eva_support: FYI customer AcmeCorp -> embeddings endpoint sometimes returns a parse error when input contains backslashes and unicode sequences. They repro with this payload:

```json
{ "input": "He said \"Hello\" and path C:\\Users\\joe\\docs\nNewline", "model": "text-embed-001" }
```

They call via SDK v0.9.2. Customer says sometimes we return 502 and the response body is "invalid JSON: unexpected backslash at position 24". Ticket 12345.

support-bot: created ticket #12345 (priority: P2)

sam_engineer: @eva_support can you paste the full curl (headers + body) and the response body? Also did they set any structured_output or pass JSON strings inside JSON?

acme_integration_engineer: here's the curl we used:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_ME" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"He said \"Hello\" and path C:\\Users\\joe\\docs\nNewline","model":"text-embed-001"}'
```

Response (502):

```json
{"error":"ParseError: invalid JSON: unexpected backslash at position 25","request_id":"req_7b2f0a"}
```

sam_engineer: looks like double-escaping: the path had \\ in the JSON but the backend tried to unescape again. SDK v0.9.2 had a regression where we JSON.stringify() on already-escaped strings when sending via the node client. @mike_sdk do we have a patch?

mike_sdk: yes, we shipped a fix in 0.9.3 that avoids serializing twice. We also added an opt `send_raw_text: true` to the client so callers can opt out of additional escaping. Recommend trying 0.9.3 or using curl with a raw body as a quick workaround.

jess_billing: fyi billing saw several calls in the window. Some failed but still logged usage; we'll need request_id(s) to reconcile. @acme_integration_engineer can you share req_7b2f0a and any others?

acme_integration_engineer: we saw req_7b2f0a and req_7b2f0b, both 502. Logs attached on our side show lots of Windows path strings. We can try the SDK upgrade but customer is production-critical.

sam_engineer: short-term workaround: base64-encode input on client, send metadata encoding: base64, and we'll decode server-side before embedding. Example payload:

```json
{"input_b64":"SGUgc2FpZC4uLg==","encoding":"base64"}
```

I'll open a fix PR for the node SDK and add tests for Windows path strings + unicode escapes. Also adding a rollback route to surface a clearer message for parse failures.

eva_support: thanks. I'll send the customer the temp workaround + ticket update. ETA to ship SDK patch to customers: today EOD.

mike_sdk: PR created: #4529. QA passed on integration. Rolling patch to staging now.

jess_billing: noted. After patch, please confirm whether those failed calls should be reclassified for billing.

acme_integration_engineer: thanks all, trying workaround now. Will report back in 30m :thumbsup:
